key_insight: CA-WCP adds class-aware, asymmetric conformal bounds to 3D segmentation so uncertainty better matches class-specific over- and under-segmentation under distribution shift.
clinical_relevance: This could make volumetric tumor and organ segmentation outputs more reliable to interpret, especially when models face data shifts and need calibrated uncertainty for reporting.
method: Uses latent-space density-ratio weighting to handle covariate shift.
Applies directional lower/upper quantiles instead of symmetric intervals.
Scales bounds with class-specific asymmetry factors from validation false-positive/false-negative rates.
evidence_signal: On BraTS 2020 and a synthetic multi-organ CT benchmark, CA-WCP achieved class-wise observed coverage whose 95% Clopper-Pearson intervals included the nominal 90% target, with interval widths 8-14% smaller than symmetric weighted conformal prediction.
watch_item: The approach depends on reliable validation-set error estimates and shift weighting, so performance may vary if the calibration data are small, noisy, or poorly matched to deployment conditions.
paper_title: Quantifying Volumetric Risk: Class-Aware Asymmetric Weighted Conformal Prediction for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
